body:
I've been having this issue as well and took a look at what it might take to fix it. 

The MustBeVariantAnalyzer checks every type argument list to see if its parent symbol (a method or a named type) has the [MustBeVariant] attribute on any of the types in its type parameter list. This does not work properly for methods defined within an extension block with a type parameter list, since the type parameters are not present in the method's symbol, only the generated extension type's symbol. This causes analysis to fail because the analyzer requires that the method symbol has more than 0 type parameters and fails if it does not.

If the extension method does have its own type parameter list, analysis will work but be done incorrectly with the extension block's type arguments being analyzed as if they were for the type parameter at the same index in the method's type parameter list. This can be seen by giving the [MustBeVariant] attribute to the first type parameter of the method but not the extension block- any uses of the method will fail when the extension block's type argument is not a variant and will succeed incorrectly when the method's type argument isn't a variant.

The best way to fix this would be to access the method symbol's AssociatedExtensionImplementation property to retrieve the extension block's type parameters to analyze, but since Godot.SourceGenerators only uses C# 12 and the AssociatedExtensionImplementation property wasn't added until C# 14, this isn't possible without upgrading both the target version of the assembly and the version of Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces. I attempted doing this, but at some point Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces started making it an error for GeneratorExecutionContext to be used by analyzers, which makes it incompatible with a lot of other code in the project. 

It seems like fixing this in the most logically correct way would require upgrading, but due to the compatibility issues I don't think there's an easy path to doing that. There could be another way handle this case in the meantime but it could potentially cause issues with false positives since there's no way to conclusively tell if something is an extension implementation.
